data.one_liner: A fully typed Dart SDK to access the Open-Meteo weather, air quality, and climate APIs.
data.what_it_does: Provides API clients for all Open-Meteo services including weather, historical data, air quality, marine conditions, and geocoding. It supports type-safe requests via FlatBuffers as well as raw JSON responses.
use_when: You need weather, climate, or air quality data in a Dart or Flutter application.
You want type-safe API responses using FlatBuffers for performance.
avoid_when: You require real-time bidirectional weather streaming via WebSockets.
You need a backend database or device storage for weather caching.
strengths: Full typed support with enums and DateTime conversions for Open-Meteo parameters.
Supports multiple locations and segmented responses in a single request.
Optimized performance using FlatBuffers under the hood.
weaknesses: Geocoding and Elevation APIs are limited to JSON response methods.
Strictly bound to the Open-Meteo service ecosystem.
data.setup_notes: No special native setup or build_runner required.

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a general-purpose HTTP client for custom REST APIs instead of a dedicated Open-Meteo SDK.

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want to make low-level HTTP requests to the Open-Meteo API manually without a wrapper SDK.
